editorial.headline: The Technical Work Behind a Managed Ship
editorial.standfirst: A ship-management activity spanning upkeep, docking preparation, crewing and maritime administration, open nationally to full foreign ownership and unblocked by Bali’s stated moratorium.
editorial.body:
Ship management is not simply the administrative afterlife of a vessel. This activity covers technical ship-management services: maintenance; preparing a ship for docking; arranging spare parts and provisions; crewing; and handling insurance and marine-certification administration. Together, those duties describe a practical operating function—keeping the technical and documentary sides of a vessel’s management in order. The breadth matters. The scope is defined by work around the ship itself, from physical upkeep and docking preparation to the arrangements that support its crew, supplies, insurance and maritime certification.

It is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That is useful not because it turns technical management into a generic business, but because it makes clear that the classification is available across the stated scale range. A registrant should therefore be offering the listed management services, rather than treating the category as a catch-all description for any maritime venture. The detail in the scope points to a service business organised around maintenance, docking preparation, spares, provisions, crewing, insurance administration and maritime-certification administration.

Nationally, the PMA status is open and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, foreign participation is permitted nationally up to full ownership under the record’s national PMA position. That clarity should not be confused with a claim about operations beyond the stated services: the national reading applies to this particular technical ship-management activity and to the scale options recorded for it. The relevant point for a foreign-owned business is direct: nationally, the activity is open, with a ceiling of 100% foreign ownership.

Bali requires a separate reading, but not a pessimistic one. This activity is not blocked for PMA registration there by the provincial moratorium. The record identifies the reason: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, rather than a Low or Medium-Low category. The moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali on a permanent, island-wide basis; this activity falls outside that stated block. Bali’s status is therefore OK or Higher Risk: it remains unblocked under the moratorium, while the recorded risk observation at the Besar scale explains why. That is the honest local position—open nationally and not barred in Bali by this moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the activity is open to full foreign ownership, and Bali does not block it under the stated moratorium.
